title: Enterprise capacity intake interview script and decision matrix
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: Create a reproducible, conversation-driven intake script and a compact decision matrix that product managers and solutions engineers can use during customer scoping calls for Dedicated capacity. Scope: enterprise requests for reserved throughput, SLA targets, GPU class preferences, burst/burst-credit policies, and scaling constraints. Deliverables: 1) A step-by-step interview script with conditional branches for common customer patterns (batch vs low-latency, regulated workloads, offline/on-prem requirements). 2) A one-page decision matrix that maps answers to recommended capacity contract terms (GPU family, reserved QPS/token throughput, canary rollout policy, allowed burst). 3) Example filled intake forms for three archetypes (High-throughput inference API, Low-latency chat product, Regulated on-prem deployment). Acceptance criteria: - PMs/SEs can complete intake in a 45-60 minute call and produce a recommended contract draft. - At least two pilot customers (internal or external) approve the recommendation flow. - Hand-off checklist for Sales/Customer Success created with gating questions and required artifacts.
interview_script: Opening: confirm stakeholders, expected decision timeline, and NDA/data constraints.
Workload profile: describe typical request types (chat/generation, embeddings, rerank, batching), token sizes, and request distribution (p90/p99 lengths).
Traffic pattern: average RPS, peak RPS, diurnal patterns, expected growth over 3/12 months, and acceptable degradation during bursts.
Latency SLOs: required p50/p90/p99 latencies for production vs batch/async paths. Ask for example SLAs they must meet to their customers.
Throughput guarantees: required reserved tokens/sec or concurrent sessions; distinguish between sustained vs burst requirements.
Model constraints: preferred model families, open vs licensed models, tolerance for quantized/FP16 variants, and expectations on deterministic outputs.
GPU preferences & constraints: any hardware restrictions (A100/H100/3090/Trn1), on-prem hardware compatibility, or affinity requirements.
Scaling policy: desired autoscaling behavior, pre-warm strategies, cold-start sensitivity, and allowable scaling latency.
Fallback & degradation: acceptable fallback models/routes, graceful degradation policies, and data loss tolerances.
Security & compliance: data residency, encryption at rest/in-transit, KMS/HSM requirements, audit log retention, and SOC/ISO requirements.
Operational readiness: SRE contact, on-call expectations, observability needs (traces, token-level cost breakdown), and runbook handoff.
Costs & commitments: target committed spend window (monthly/annual), preferred billing cadence, and flexibility for burst credits.
Close: summarize recommended next steps, request sample traffic logs or replay dataset, and schedule technical deep-dive if approved.
decision_matrix: If latency SLO p99 <= 200ms AND peak RPS <= 500 -> recommend single-region A100/H100 pool with 2x headroom, reserved throughput = 1.5 * peak baseline.
If workload is batch-only (jobs with >5s tolerance) -> recommend high-density GPU family + aggressive autoscaler and batch-batching with KV cache offloading.
If regulated (data residency + KMS) -> recommend Private/VPC deployment, include HSM/KMS integration line item, and require security_review_required true in contract.
If customer prefers deterministic outputs and will not accept quantized artifacts -> recommend FP16/FP32 model tiers, add quality regression clause and evaluation runway.
If expected growth >3x in 3 months -> recommend burst credit pool and a staged commit (baseline reserved + burstable capacity with spending cap).
If customer cannot tolerate >1 minute of scaling latency -> recommend pre-warmed standby nodes and canary traffic routing for rollouts.
If peak token throughput is spiky (short windows with 10-20x baseline) -> recommend multi-region routing + burst credits and fallback to smaller, cheaper models for non-critical routes.
If customer requests on-prem -> include upgrade window constraints, image signing requirements, and a maintenance SLA addendum.
archetype_examples: High-throughput inference API: peak 7k RPS, p99 latency tolerance 500ms, recommend dedicated A100 pool with autoscaler and token-throttling policy.
Low-latency chat product: p99 <= 150ms, recommend smaller batch sizes, hot KV caching, and pre-warmed H100 nodes; reserved throughput sized at 1.25 * p99 traffic to account for headroom.
Regulated on-prem legal-doc processing: on-prem deployment, KMS/HSM required, conservative FP32 model variants, and rolling upgrades with test windows.
handoff_checklist: Completed intake script and filled decision matrix PDF/Drive link.
Sample traffic replays (S3 link) or synthetic generator configuration.
Security/compliance artifacts: SOC2, encryption requirements, and contact for customer security review.
Proposed draft contract with reserved throughput, burst policy, pricing band, and upgrade cadence.
Technical deep-dive scheduled with engineering + SEs (date/time).
